txt: A loud sigh fills the channel. "We will hear your request, Firewalker, although we must inform you that the Committee does not typically intervene in *personal* matters..."
A moment of stunned silence. "How did you know that?"
A sigh. "You are thinking about this metaphor too literally..."
She laughs. "Do we sound like we're from Sur-la-Clef to you?"
You think you hear a faint sigh coming from the other end of the connection...

"'Personal business'? We aren't sure you understand. The Committee is waiting for you. You have to tell them what you've uncovered about. The stakes here are *much* greater than any 'personal business' you may be working through..."

"*Extremely different*. We knew there were still parts of Revachol that have not fully recovered from the Revolution, but here the destruction is quite evident, even compared to the eastern side of the city..."
"*Subito*. Coalition Shuttle Laurel is setting a course for your position. They will arrive momentarily. Stand by..."
"... Firewalker? Are you there?"
"... We're afraid we must ask you to repeat that, Firewalker."
"... nothing important, bad connection... Going to update the receiving frequency..."
"... of course, serving on a Coalition warship does require some *personal* sacrifices, but we have to be willing to make them, if we believe in the mission..."
"... six-weeks paid leave, bilingual childcare, vocational certification credits. Really, it's quite a good career."
"A roundabout, a roundabout..."
"A state is like any other living thing -- it wants to survive and grow. A state that doesn't value its own existence is not a state at all."
"A very important question with a very simple answer: We want humanity to endure."
"A very important question. The wings are carefully selected to represent a wide spectrum of political thought."
"About 3,000 years."
"Acknowledged. But there's still something we don't understand: Did you speak with the victim *before* his death?"
"Acknowledged. Laurel has initiated the extraction procedure. Stand by..."
"Acknowledged. Listen very carefully, Firewalker. We are going to ask you a series of questions. It is imperative that you answer as directly and truthfully as you can. Do you understand?"
"Acknowledged. Please stand by while we transmit our summary to the Committee..."
"Acknowledged. To reach the Committee, all you need to do is fill out the appropriate request form and submit it to the liaison for public affairs."
"Acknowledged. We are at your disposal."
"Ah! What a difference a few well-designed market incentives can make. And, of course, it is important for the RCM to set an example."
"Ah, that must be. We have only recently been detailed to the Archer, so we are still learning the names of all the many districts..."
"Ah, there are children building a snowman by a small pond. The homes and gardens are quite beautiful, very near like those in certain areas of Messina."
"Ah, there are children playing by a small pond. The homes and gardens are quite beautiful, very near like those in certain areas of Messina."
"Ah, there are children running home to get out of the rain. The homes and gardens are quite beautiful, very near like those in certain areas of Messina."
"Ah, we are looking at a great river now. This must be the Esperance. It's very nice, actually..."
"Ah, we see. You are playing a practical joke. Very funny..."
"Ah, well, we see the many, hmmm, *historic* buildings, of course, and the snow gathering along the rim of the bay..."
"Ah, yes. The birdwatching here is very lovely. We saw a pair of great skuas on the wing earlier today."
"Almost certainly. Not many realise this, but, the Moralintern is constantly reviewing and revising its contingency spreads in order to improve our own decision-making..."
"And *how* do you know this?"
"And *what* did it say, exactly?"
"And now, we are updating our frequencies. We will not speak again. This connection will be cleared in four... three..."

"And then there are our prodigal cousins, the Vaasan social democrats, who hold our same values and have even adopted many of our same rites and iconography, though they persist in rejecting the umbrella of moralism."
"And then there's all the *tare* lying about. It's very unpleasant to look at. We're going to widen our viewfinder a bit."
"And therein lies their danger. They 'feel' true without *being* true..."
"Answer the question, please."
"At the same time, the RCM is not exactly *of* the Coalition."
"Because it's standard practice for signallers to use the *pluralis officialis* during the course of our duties. It's meant to serve as a reminder that we don't speak only for ourselves."
"Because no rational state is willing to accept the risk of such a calamity befalling its own people, all powers are incentivised to *de-escalate* conflicts before they reach the point of no return."

"Because the Coalition has no interest in *running* Revachol. We'll succeed in our mission the moment Revachol rejoins the international community as a sovereign democracy. The RCM is an integral piece of that project."

"Because what you are saying makes no sense. From the sound of your voice, it appears that you have been under the influence of alcohol. It is our recommendation that you speak with your station lazareth *immediately* about treatment options..."

"Because what you're saying suggests that you are experiencing an acute psychic break with reality. You don't need to speak with the Committee, you need to speak with your station lazareth, *immediately*..."

"Because you're speaking like someone in the throes of a serious drug addiction. Your words have no connection to reality. You don't need to speak with the Committee, you need to speak with your station lazareth, *immediately*..."
"Beyond that, it may be said that we are the inheritors and stewards of Dolores Dei's legacy."

"But as the sun sets, the shadows cast by those columns and arcades weave together to form an intricate umbral lattice. When you see it, you suddenly understand: It was all built for you, for *this very moment*."
"But in a practical sense, it's the responsibility of the Ethics Division to ensure that both organisations are working toward the same ends."
"But it's a delicate and very complicated subject. And of course every belief system has something to recommend it."
"But now we have gotten quite far afield. What was your request?"
"But now we seem to be quite turned about. We'll have to consult a map in the future. Now, was there something else?"
"But now we've wandered quite far afield. What was your request?"
"But of course, they also remain dependable partners in a number of centrist governing coalitions."
"But one must consider that the world was in the midst of a global catastrophe brought on by an unstoppable pandemic. No amount of contingency planning could account for *all of that*."
"But to the north is all water..."
"But we must stress that real democracy is an ongoing process and not simply an outcome. It must be cultivated and preserved if it is to endure."
"But we shouldn't overstate their importance. They are simply one of many tools used by the Moralintern to set policy."
"But what's most striking are the people. They just... we don't even know how to say it..."
"By thousands of people over many centuries, in keeping with a precise plan each believed in but never expected to see the final completion of..."
"Come again, Firewalker? You're saying that the victim was killed in some sort of... romantic imbroglio?"
"Come again, Firewalker? You're saying the victim was killed by communists? Was this a politically motivated homicide?"
"Come again? Something 'miraculous,' you say?"
"Come again? We are picking up more interference..."
"Enough jokes, then. What was your request?"
"Esattamente. But the Commission's hard and diligent work may soon be bearing fruit: Revachol is nearly ready to begin the first phase of democratisation."
"Esattamente."
"Even though we are only a second signaller, we can tell you with great certainty that there is no contingency spread for you, Firewalker."
"Final question: Were you alone?"
"Firewalker, are you still there?"
"Firewalker, surely you are aware that it is a civil offence to maliciously or frivolously obstruct a Coalition radio frequency..."
"Firewalker, this is Archer. Are you there?"
"Firewalker, this is Coalition Warship Archer, please acknowledge."
"Firewalker, this is Coalition Warship Archer. We are acknowledging and accepting you."
"Firewalker, this is Coalition Warship Archer. We have been instructed to inform you that the Laurel arrived at your position. Please acknowledge."
"Firewalker, this is a very serious claim. Please describe the situation as succinctly as possible. We will forward your summary to the Committee."
"Firewalker, was there anything else?"
"Firewalker, we must be perfectly honest with you: We cannot recommend that you address the Committee, not under the present circumstances, at least..."
"Firewalker... can you... what do you mean?"
"Firewalker... please repeat... your signal is *very* weak..."

"For instance, as second signaller we represent Coalition Warship Archer, which in turn represents INSURCOM and the Coalition more generally, which in turn represents the Moralist International, which itself represents the interests of 1.2 billion people across the world."
"For the most part, it has. The world is certainly not free of violent conflict, but in the modern era we have made great strides to reduce its frequency, duration, and severity."
"For this reason, responsibility for developing contingency spreads is only assigned to highly trained analysts working with advanced radiocomputers and a steady supply of drouamine."
"For you, for all of humanity..."
"Fortunately, we have contingency spreads to help guide our decision making."
"From here all we can really see are his enormous muttonchops. Perhaps he is some sort of motorcyclist?"
"From here all we can really see are his pale cheeks. He looks like he hasn't slept in days."
"Gardeners and lawyers are both essential to a beautiful and well-functioning society, but we're referring to something else..."
"Good god. Is there anything else the Committee should know?" You hear the sound of a page turning, followed by fierce scribbling.
"Good. First question: Are you currently in the vicinity of Sereglee, the North Arcade Islands, or Near Pale Offshore Platform 'Insulindico'?"
"History is a river coursing ever downward. Occasionally its course is redirected in mysterious and unexpected ways."
"Hmmm, that's difficult to say. We have a very particular view from our observation platform up here."
"Hmmm. Was there anything else the Committee should know?" If she's writing, you can't hear anything.
"Hold on. We're adjusting our viewfinder..."
"How curious. You learn the most interesting things on these sorts of assignments."
"How interesting. In Messina, disco has been extinct for more than a decade. Funny how the past always seems more present in some parts of the world."
"However you feel about weaponry as such, it is one of the great technical achievements of the modern era."
"I... We don't appreciate whatever game you're playing, Firewalker. Now, what is your request?"

"I... cannot say we agree, speaking for a moment in strictly personal terms. You have convinced us that the situation in Martinaise is untenable, but we are only the second signaller, and there is no appealing the Committee's decision..."
"If by 'fun stuff,' you mean alcohol and cigarettes, that's true. Actually, we don't even have Fritttes where we're from. In Messina they're called Averros..."

"If the liaison accepts your request, you will be invited to address the Committee at their next quarterly public hearing. We believe the next hearing is scheduled for July." She seems very satisfied by this answer.
"If you believe so strongly in your own destiny that the rest of reality exists only as a warped reflection of it, how can it be contradicted?"
"If you had, then you would remember. It is one of the great wonders of the world, impossible to mistake or forget."

"Immeasurable. It includes interisolary travel, three scientific revolutions, humanism, internationalism, the welfare state, and *balance of terror theory*. Nothing less than the intellectual foundation of our modern order."
"Impossible to say for certain. Human beings are notoriously bad at predicting all the different ways events might unravel..."
"In Messina, of course. Not only was it the site of Dolores Dei's crowning, it was also one of the great cities of the Dolorian era, a glorious expression of humanity's highest potential..."
"In any event, it is certainly interesting to see you, even from afar. Most of the time, we signallers just have to *imagine* what our interlocutors look like."
"In any event, thank you for this *tour* of Revachol West. It has certainly been... educational."
"In fact, you may have picked the perfect time to get involved: Revachol is nearly ready to begin the first phase of democratisation."
"In most cases, the Provisional Council selects them from a cross-section of the local population to ensure the slates actually reflect the people they represent."
"Interesting. The west of the city looks *very* different from the east. There's a large motorway dividing it nearly in half. This must be the 8/81, no?"
"Interesting. We don't know much about Revacholian art, so you'll have to forgive our ignorance."
"Is everything alright? We lost the connection for a moment..."
"Is everything alright?"
"It all depends on your perspective."
"It appears to go on for quite a while. There's a heavily industrialised district that seems to abut Monte-Martin..."
"It does, doesn't it? And yet there remains a great deal to be done in that span."
"It is a work-in-progress, but it is also the best way that humanity has found thus far."
"It is in all senses the most moderate and reasonable projection possible based on current science."
"It is one of the most advanced currently in service. Capable of firing fifty rounds per minute along twenty co-aligned arcs..."
"It is possible. We grew up there. We have seen the lattice with our own eyes."
"It is quite striking, compared to where we're from. There are a great many destroyed buildings, *still*. And we don't see any horses... It's really *nothing* like the eastern side of the city..."
"It may be a *demanding* job, but the Coalition is committed to ensuring those in its service maintain a healthy work-life balance..."

"It may be the case that, under certain scenarios, Revachol is vitally important, as it was during the Coalition landings in '08. It may also be the case in many other equally plausible scenarios that Revachol is simply another once-great city, like countless others throughout history."
"It may be. We're only a second signaller, not a metaphysician. It's a rather cold way to think about the world, isn't it?"
"It must be. Unfortunately we do not have time to hear it just now."

"It was established by many of the same Founding Party members who elected Dolores Dei, and who, after her assassination, dedicated their lives to the continuation of her political and intellectual project."
"It's a great honour and responsibility. In addition to monitoring public frequencies, we are tasked with maintaining some of the most sensitive communications equipment aboard the Archer."

"It's an elegant idea, one of the cornerstones of the modern era. In short, it holds that durable, lasting peace is possible when the major powers are capable of inflicting unacceptable and irreversible destruction upon one another..."
"It's an important responsibility, but we don't consider it any greater than those borne by countless people all across the world..."
"It's completely natural. Studies have shown that the untrained mind is only capable of considering so many possibilities in place at once, usually no more than three or four..."
"It's even possible the cities that will resolve the questions of the future have not been founded yet."
"It's not really our area of expertise, but we can try to explain. Picture a smooth hill made from fresh dirt. Now, if you stand atop this hill and pour a glass of water over it, what will happen?"
"It's our understanding that the RCM's organisational structure predates the Coalition. We believe it may even be modelled after the communard brigades themselves."
"Let us answer your question with a question: Have you ever seen evening fall over the old town of Advesperascit?"
"Local matters can wait. Coalition Shuttle Laurel is setting a course for your position. They will arrive momentarily. Stand by..."

"Many political theorists have argued that communism accepts the logic of Dolorian humanism while abandoning its spirit. They offer a cautionary tale, in other words, about attempting to found a paradise atop bones and ashes..."
"Martinaise, Martinaise... That is to the west, yes?"
"Mhmm. Let's go on..."
"Mhmmm... ah. So *that* is Martinaise..."
"Never mind that. All you need to do is repeat what you just said..."
"Next question: At the time, did you experience *sense objects*?"
"No -- well, not quite. The Moralintern never *intends* to violate another nation's sovereignty. That would be a serious violation of international law..."
"No, Firewalker, we did not."

"No, of course not. There are many nations outside the Moralintern's umbrella, in Seol, Samara, and elsewhere. At most you might say the Moralintern represents between a quarter and a third of humanity."
"No, that cannot be right. That way is only sprawl. We were under the impression that Martinaise was nearer to the Bay..."
"No, the captain of the Archer is deeply classified intelligence. We are the second signaller."
"Not a problem. If this is a *time-sensitive* matter, you may file an emergency address request with the liaison for public affairs."
"Not exactly. No one can know the future. But with contingency spreads it is possible to predict what the future realities *might reasonably* look like."

"Not only that, but you, you are also part of that centuries-long plan. When you cross one of the open plazas, your own shadow is effortlessly woven into the great latticework, a deliberate synthesis of humanity, art, and the natural world."
"Nothing remarkable. Really, we have been very fortunate. But we do sometimes wonder what we might be missing out on, back in Messina..."

"Now we see the lake, and around that a rather vibrant-looking city quarter. There are some large buildings, from the turn-of-the-century, we would guess. Yes, this must be the heart of the district."
"Now, please dispense with the games, Firewalker. This is a public frequency..."
"Now, please excuse us while we update the receiving frequency. This connection will be cleared in four... three..."
"Now, the first signaller has informed us that we must update the receiving frequency. This connection will be cleared in four... three..."
"Now... your request?"
"Of course not. It's simply a rhetorical convention, a common synecdoche. We are the second signaller."
"Of course not. The Moralintern is committed to giving every person the opportunity to flourish..."

"Of course, such a city does not spring from nowhere, nor does it endure without effort. Its construction was the work of many generations, and its preservation is an equally monumental responsibility."
"Of course, such a situation is not ideal. We would all prefer for Revacholians to nominate their representatives directly. But that is why it's a transitional council."
"Of course, the number 3,000 represents the average of a great number of projections. The actual number might be closer to 2,800 or even 2,750, depending on the contingencies..."
"Of course, the number 3,000 represents the average of a great number of projections. The actual number might be closer to 3,250 or even 3,300, depending on the contingencies..."
"Of course, there is no one spread that can reasonably account for all these possible events. But at least we're able to prepare for the most likely eventualities."
"Of course. This is history we're talking about."
"Of course. We're only a second signaller, not a metaphysician. We sometimes find it overwhelming also..."

"Of course. While the content of individual contingency spreads is deeply classified, many degrees beyond our access, everything we have heard from the Provisional Commission indicates that the transition is proceeding according to the appropriate timetable."
"Oh, *incomparably* so, but that isn't what made her so remarkable."
"Oh, it looks quite lovely from here, even with the rain. From our porthole, we see rolling hillsides, a public park filled with grand oak trees, men and women going about on horses..."
"Oh, it looks quite lovely from here. From our porthole, we see rolling hillsides covered with snow, a public park filled with grand oak trees, men and women going about on horses..."
"Oh, it looks quite lovely from here. From our porthole, we see rolling hillsides, a public park filled with grand oak trees, men and women going about on horses..."
"Oh, it's fine..."
"Oh, most likely. Though of course it depends on the contingencies."

"Oh, there are many things you can do. If you're interested in learning how to canvass for signatures, manage a polling place, or register voters, the Commission would be more than happy to direct you to a workshop..."
"Oh, yes, we could always use more time off." She laughs politely, but doesn't elaborate.
"Once elected, council members will even have the opportunity to join one of several officially sanctioned political wings, depending on their ideological beliefs and policy preferences."
"One now committed to upholding moralist values. Strange, isn't it?"
"Only in the sense that the entire world has to 'wing' its way through history. The Moralintern simply aims to 'wing it' as little as possible..."
"Our best theoreticians believe that three to five phases are appropriate for states that lack strong democratic traditions, which would certainly apply to Revachol."
"Our concerns exist on the scale of decades, centuries, and millennia. Sometimes we say the Moralintern worries about the future so that normal people may worry about today."
"Our name is not important. All you need to know is that we hold the position of second signaller aboard the Archer."
"Perhaps the best way to describe it is to say we have a *very wide perspective*, but not an especially detailed one."
"Perhaps you are confused as to the scale on which the contingency spreads function..."
"Perhaps you are in a different part of the city? We have only recently been detailed to the Archer, so we are still learning the names of all the many districts..."

"Perhaps you could say that we represent the interests and hopes of a great many people, but you could say just as easily that we are the assistant to the secretary of a factotum, no more remarkable than the lowest cashier of a common Frittte..."

"Perhaps, perhaps not. Could the Perikarnassians have foreseen the role Revachol would play in events to come? In truth, history only appears to rhyme because we cannot perceive events in their full complexity..."
"Perhaps? We do not generally reach for such *evocative imagery*, but there is something rather desperate about them."
"Please acknowledge. What do you mean 'the world is going to end'?"
"Please answer the question."
"Please be advised that you are speaking on the public frequency. What is your request?"
"Please confirm. Are you saying your partner is somehow *impeding* your investigation?"
"Please continue. We're listening." You can hear her furiously scribbling notes...
"Please understand, we are not some totalitarian enterprise. We are committed to and bound by the highest values of individual freedom and opportunity."

"Precisamente. We know only that it will run down, but not what course it will take. If we place a rock in the water's path, will it divert to the left or the right? We cannot say, but we may predict which way it might run in either event..."
"Quite good. We enjoy all the standard benefits for Moralintern forces on active duty assignments: Excellent healthcare, foreign service pay, a fully funded pension system..."

"Real democracy doesn't just happen. It requires the support of a great number of stable, interlocking institutions. *That* is the only way to channel popular sentiment into a legitimate mandate to govern. Otherwise, what are we left with?"
"Really, it's not important. We would strongly prefer that you state your request."
"Really? It seems quite important. It may be the largest road in the city..."
"Remain where you are. Coalition Shuttle Laurel is setting a course for your position. They will arrive momentarily. Stand by..."
"Repeat that, Firewalker? What do you mean 'you can't'? Are you being impeded in some way?"
"She was the greatest innocence, the single most consequential being to have ever lived. Her legacy touches every aspect of modern life."
"She was. There are even those who say that Advesperascit *summoned* Dolores Dei, or that it was built in preparation for her, centuries before her arrival..."
"Simply that there is no such thing as an individual contingency spread..."
"So you're experiencing acute memory loss. We don't see how this is the Committee's business."
"Soon, the people of Revachol will vote for slates of candidates who will make up the transitional advisory council that will oversee the second phase of democratisation."
"Specifically, they said that 'disputes of purely local concern' do not fall under their purview..."
"Stand by a moment... we are adjusting our viewfinder..."
"Strange... we see the roundabout, and the monument, but... the horse seems to be *missing* its head... and there's a man *on top of it*?"
"Thank you for standing by. We are authorised to report the Committee of Responsibility for Revachol has acknowledged *and accepted* your request."
"Thank you, Firewalker. Please stand by while we transmit our summary..."
"Thank you. The Committee of Responsibility for Revachol has authorised us to offer you an immediate extraction. Do you accept?"
"That depends on how you look at it. Since the Perikarnassian Incident, there have been nearly 8,000 years of recorded history..."

"That is extremely admirable. Of course, the Coalition supports the Revacholian people's desire for full democracy. We encourage you to contact the offices of the Provisional Commission if you are serious about getting involved."
"That is the essence of the idea. You might also imagine these spreads as a kind of tree, with every juncture representing a different event, and every branch representing a different timeline."
"That is the nature of the command pyramid, yes. Most modern organisations work in a similar way, even the RCM."
"That must be a Martinaise custom. You'll have to forgive our ignorance. We are still relatively new here."
"That's *you*? We have to say, that's extremely irregular, Firewalker. What are you doing on top of that public monument?"
"That's certainly possible. Though of course it depends on the contingencies."
"That's correct. But we must say that it has been... *interesting* to speak with you. If nothing else, the RCM is frequently a source of curiosity to those of us aboard the Archer."
"That's impossible to say. It may be that Revachol has a great role to play, or no role at all. That is the nature of contingencies."
"That's why the old town is sometimes called 'The Ceremonial Heart of Humanity'..."
"That's... rather optimistic. Though of course it depends on the contingencies."
"The Moralintern is not Seol. There is no secret vault of files beneath Isherwood or La Cherte or anywhere else, because that is not the Moralintern's purpose..."
"The RCM exists under the umbrella of the Coalition, just as the Coalition exists under the umbrella of the Moralintern..."
"The chief signaller, our superior. They are ultimately responsible for all communications aboard the Archer..."

"The council is modelled after similar bodies developed in a number of transitional democracies. Its role is to devise and shape the future institutions of Revacholian democracy, according to local conditions..."

"The fascists say they are *both* the ancestors of and the successors to Dolorianism. In other words, they believe that Dolores Dei's reign simply represents a glorious phase of expansion within a greater Franconigerian heritage. They criticise the Dolorian project for accepting and integrating new peoples rather than forcefully subjugating them..."
"The first phase of democratisation."

"The heart of the city, the old town, is a district composed of weathered marble, comprising thousands of columns and arcades arranged around a series of grand plazas. During the day it's a beautiful sight, equal to any of the great cities of Perikarnassis."
"The key, we believe, is to be open to meaning even amidst great uncertainty. But now we are only speaking for ourselves."

"The point is that we know only that the water will run down, but not what course it will take. If we place a rock in the water's path, will it divert to the left or the right? We cannot say, but we may predict which way it might run in either event..."

"The role of the Moralist International is two-fold, to buy humanity sufficient time to perfect itself, and to patiently guide it along the road while protecting it from ideological highwaymen and eschatologians."
"Then we are not sure what assistance can be rendered. This is quite beyond the purview of the Committee of Responsibility..."
"Then we recommend you speak with your station lazareth. This has nothing to do with the Committee of Responsibility..."
"Then you would like being on an aerostatic, there's always *something* that must be done..."
"There are a few people on horses by a small pond. The homes and gardens are quite beautiful, very near like those in certain areas of Messina."
"There are also a number of seabirds looping and twisting in the wind below us. No horses, though... And of course we can see some people, but they, oh, how to say it..."

"There are many. The communists say they are the next dialectical step in an inexorable spiral of progress. They claim to have resolved the 'inherent contradictions' of moralism and believe they're just one revolution away from establishing a humanist paradise..."
"There are people who say that, but we've never felt that way. To us they look like miniature figures, the kind you see in model train sets. But this... this is a *very sad* train set."
"They added that they expect the RCM to fulfil its responsibilities 'to a high degree of satisfaction'..."
"They typically respond within a few weeks."
"They would like you to address your matter to the Committee *directly*, at their earliest convenience."
"This is why it is critical for the international community to work toward peace and cooperation between nations. There's simply too much at stake."
"This is... Warship Archer. We are acknowledging and accepting you... though we're still getting quite a bit of interference..."
"To be completely honest, Firewalker, we are not in a position to say. We can't really make out *faces* from this distance..."
"To the south. Let us see..."
"Two... one... 'Après le monde, le gris'..."

"Typically, there's a liberal technocratic wing, a social democratic wing, and even a conservative populist wing. You wouldn't believe some of the ideas they express! But a vibrant and free political culture requires that all perspectives be given voice, even those many may find objectionable."
"Unfortunately we cannot accept your request. We really have no idea what you are talking about, but we're quite sure it is beyond the purview of the Committee of Responsibility..."
"Very good. Next question: Would you describe the phenomenon as *internal* to the isola, or *external* to the isola?"
"Very well. Now we are looking at an area that seems to be in urgent need of *revitalisation*..."
"Viewed from that perspective, we are nearly three-quarters of the way there."
"Watch your tone. Now, please describe the situation in as much detail as you can. We will forward our summary to the Committee."
"We are far past that point, Firewalker. There is only one question now: Are you ready, or are you not?"
"We are living in the only reality we know. Our task is to make the best of it that we can..."
"We are sorry to hear of your loss, but personal tragedy is quite beyond the purview of the Committee of Responsibility..."
"We ask you one more time. Are you prepared to accept your responsibility?"
"We can assure you your partner will carry on just fine, that is his responsibility, just as this is yours. Now, there's no time to waste. The Committee is waiting to hear what you've uncovered..."
"We can assure you, it is coming as soon as possible."
"We cannot say for certain. East, it must be? We have only recently been detailed to the Archer, so we are still learning the names of all the many districts..."
"We cannot transfer you to the Committee because we are not entrusted with that responsibility. We are simply the second signaller."
"We don't believe there is anyone younger than 70 named Eleanora..."
"We don't resent them. It's more that we are... *disappointed* that they have chosen to emphasise certain points of dispute over broad areas of accord..."
"We have it. Is there anything else the Committee should know?" You hear the sound of her pen scratching against paper.
"We have to say, this is *extremely* disappointing to hear, Firewalker..."
"We have transmitted our summary to the Committee of Responsibility. Please continue standing by..."
"We need to know more than that. Now, please describe the situation in as much detail as you can. We will forward our summary to the Committee."
"We really couldn't say. That's one of the limits of this vantage. But the whole district does have a very *desperate* character."
"We repeat: Were you alone?"
"We see..."
"We will pass along a summary of your report, minus any *speculative or paranatural* elements. What the Committee does from there is beyond our control..."

"We're afraid so. But we must say that it has been... *a privilege* to speak with you. You've shown yourself to be a credit to the RCM, and we wish you good fortune and safety during the course of your work."
"We're afraid that is quite impossible, Firewalker."
"We're afraid that won't be possible, Firewalker."

"We're sorry we did not come bearing better news. But we must say that it has been... *a privilege* to speak with you. We believe you are a credit to the RCM, and we wish you good fortune and safety during the course of your work."

"You're welcome. We must say that it has been... *interesting* to speak with you. If nothing else, the RCM is frequently a source of curiosity to those of us aboard the Archer."
"Your case? We aren't sure you understand. The Committee is waiting for you. You have to tell them what you've uncovered. The stakes here are *much* greater than any individual 'case'..."
